description: Table 4 rendered as an image: a two-way matrix of first-order and second-order interaction coefficients for liquid steel at 1873 K, with rows indexed by solute i and columns indexed by solute j (column headers, left to right: C, Si, Mn, P, S, Al, O, N, Ti). Five row blocks are present, in the printed order Al, N, Ti, Mn and S; each row block contains two lines — the upper line holds the first-order coefficient r_i^j printed unparenthesised, the lower line holds the second-order coefficient printed in parentheses, as defined by the caption footnote "a) (): r_i^j". Every entry carries a bracketed literature reference, mostly [24], with [23] for Al–Mn, [25]–[28] for Al second-order terms, [29]–[32] for N, [33]–[37] for Ti, [38]–[39] and [25] for Mn and S; empty cells are marked with a dash "–" and unavailable second-order values with "(–)". Representative printed values include Al–C 0.091[24] and (−0.004)[25], Al–O −6.6[24] and (39.823)[26], Ti–N −1.8[24] and (0)[36], Ti–O −1.8[24] and (−0.355)[35], Mn–C −0.07[24], and S–O −0.27[24]. The table supplies the thermodynamic interaction parameters used with the citing text to compute the theoretical AlN inclusion concentration in samples 1#–3#.

observations.observation: The table is a two-way matrix of interaction coefficients with row index i and column index j, the column headers being C, Si, Mn, P, S, Al, O, N, Ti.
Five row blocks are listed in the order Al, N, Ti, Mn, S, and each block has two lines: the upper unparenthesised first-order coefficient and the lower parenthesised second-order coefficient.
The caption defines the parenthesised lower-line notation: "a) (): r_i^j".
The caption states the tabulated first-order and second-order interaction coefficients are for 1873 K and are compiled from references [23–39].

Most entries carry the reference superscript [24]; other references used are [23] (Al–Mn first-order), [25], [26], [27], [28] (Al second-order), [29]–[32] (N second-order), [33]–[37] (Ti second-order), [38] and [39] (Mn, S second-order).
Printed Al values include Al–C 0.091[24], Al–Si 0.0056[24], Al–Mn 0[23], Al–S 0.03[24], Al–Al 0.045[24], Al–O −6.6[24] and Al–N −0.053[24].
Among the second-order entries the largest-magnitude printed value is Al–O (39.823)[26], contrasting with Al–O first-order −6.6[24].
Printed Mn values include Mn–C −0.07[24], Mn–P −0.0035[24], Mn–S −0.048[24], Mn–O −0.083[24] and Mn–N −0.091[24]; the Mn–Si and Mn–Mn first-order cells are blank (dash).
Empty cells are marked with a dash "–" and unavailable second-order coefficients with a parenthesised dash "(–)".
The citing text states that these interaction coefficients are shown in Table 4 and are used to express the theoretical concentration of AlN inclusions formed in samples 1# to 3#.

subfigures.description: Single-panel two-way table of interaction coefficients r_i^j at 1873 K. Row index i = Al, N, Ti, Mn, S (each with an upper first-order line and a parenthesised lower second-order line); column index j = C, Si, Mn, P, S, Al, O, N, Ti. Each cell is a numeric coefficient with a superscript literature citation; dashes mark absent values.
